newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh asks EU to relax shrimp import ban.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh asks EU to relax shrimp import ban.

text.p: Dhaka on Thursday asked the European Commission to relax its ban on imports of Bangladesh shrimp until the end of September.
Government officials said a formal request was made at a meeting between envoys of European Union countries and Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad.
The commission has told Bangladesh that its shrimp would not be accepted in European Union ports after August 15 on health grounds, Bangladesh's Export Promotion Bureau said.
"We have requested them to extend the deadline to September 30," Azad told a news conference.
"I told the envoys that we want to abide by the EU rules. They are sympathetic to our cause," he said.
Azad said he had asked the EU envoys to invite inspection teams to recheck conditions in Bangladesh's fish industry.
"We don't have any health concern here. There is no problem of cholera or typhoid in Bangladesh," he said.
One official said two million shrimp fishermen and others connected to the industry would be affected.
Bangladesh earns nearly $200 million a year through shrimp export to EU countries which account for 60 percent of Bangladesh's total shrimp exports.
The other main buyers are Japan and the United States.
Exporters said stocks of shrimp worth about two billion taka ($45 million) were ready at factories and ports for shipment to EU markets.

"These consignments were against firm orders. We cannot export them because they can't reach European ports by the August 15 deadline. It's a big blow to our trade," said Salauddin Ahmed, a leading exporter.
EU officials in Dhaka said the EC Veterinary Council had ordered the ban following reports by inspectors who visited Bangladesh last month.

"It's not that Bangladesh was singled out. A similar ban was considered for India and Madagascar. We have been asking Bangladesh to improve quality of shrimp processing since 1993 but they paid little heed," one EU official said.
